text:
sarah_sales: Heads up — Acme (Alice) wants an air-gapped POC in their colo next month. Key asks: signed delta bundles, 3-month upgrade cadence, customer-managed KMS/HSM, bandwidth ~50GB/week. Anyone see blockers?

mike_se: We can do minibundles + signed manifests. Need to confirm exact KMS flow — do they expect us to have remote access or for them to sign locally?

ana_infra: Packaging notes: recommend delta minibundles for weekly patches + full bundle quarterly. Big caveat: GPU/kernel driver pinning increases bundle size. 50GB/week is doable with diffs but need strict chunking.

jordan_sec: Security questionnaire flagged two redlines: (1) key escrow / vendor-controlled keys, (2) ability to perform offline signing in-customer. They insist on customer control of private keys.

alice_cust: Confirming: Acme cannot allow Redwood to hold private keys. Their SecOps prefers we provide a signing tool they can run in their HSM to sign manifests. Also want a clear rollback procedure and SLAs for patch delivery.

raj_ops: Rollback approach: include a safe-rollback script + checksums in each minibundle. Important: DB/state migrations need reversible scripts, otherwise rollback might require manual db fixes. For weekly patches we can target a 1-hour maintenance window.

mike_se: Quick feasibility: we support customer-supplied signing keys in Private deployments (BYOK) but for POC we need a simple flow. Two options: (A) provide a signing-tool container + instructions so customer signs bundles locally, or (B) ship unsigned bundles and customer sign after verification. Which do they prefer?

jordan_sec: Policy: we must never accept customer private key material. If we provide a signing tool, it must run entirely in-customer network and we should add a clause in the SOW stating Redwood never receives private keys. Legal to review.

sarah_sales: Action items: @mike_se create a minimal signing-tool container + README, include example commands and verification steps. @raj_ops draft a rollback/runbook and preflight checklist. @jordan_sec draft the legal/seq language for the SOW. @alice_cust can you confirm Acme will run the tool or require Redwood to sign within their HSM? :eyes:

alice_cust: They'll run the tool in their airgap HSM. Also asking about any incremental pricing for weekly minibundles vs. quarterly full bundles — they expect some engineering handling fee.

mike_se: Pricing note: airgap packaging is an add-on: one-time packaging fee (engineering + validation) + per-release handling fee for minibundles. For enterprise win we usually fold into a committed Dedicated package — I can propose a discount schedule in the next doc.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created ticket INF-8421 — packaging: airgap signing-tool + minibundle diff workflow.

sarah_sales: Thanks all. I'll schedule a sync with Acme for Thu 10am PT to walk through the runbook draft and pricing options. Marking blockers: KMS/HSM signing flow and rollback migration reversibility.

mike_se: I'll draft the signing-tool repo with these commands as a starting point:

```
# run inside customer network
docker run --rm -v /data/bundles:/bundles redwood/signing-tool:latest \
  sign --bundle /bundles/2025-03-minibundle.tar.gz \
  --hsm-slot 0 --key-label "acme-poc-signing" \
  --out /bundles/2025-03-minibundle.signed

# verify
redwood-verify --manifest /bundles/manifest.json --signature /bundles/2025-03-minibundle.signed
```

raj_ops: I'll add the preflight checklist: disk space, kernel/driver matrix, GPU driver pin, and dry-run verification step.

jordan_sec: I'll loop in Legal for the SOW clause and post here.

sarah_sales: Good. Recording next steps and will follow up w/ calendar invite. :thumbsup:
